articles.title: TikTok “AI-generated” label: where it comes from and how to remove it from your video
articles.desc: Why TikTok automatically labels a video as AI-generated, which data in the file triggers it, and how to clean the video before posting without losing quality.
articles.body:
TikTok automatically adds an “AI-generated” label when it finds generation records in the file. It often shows up on videos you only touched up with AI: upscaling, background removal, an effect.
## Why TikTok adds the label
- Many AI tools and editors write Content Credentials (C2PA) into the video — a signed record of how the file was made.
- TikTok reads these records on upload and turns the label on automatically.
- Files can also carry software and device tags.
## How to clean the video
- Open [@AIMediaclean_bot](https://t.me/AIMediaclean_bot?start=blog_en_tiktok) and send the clip as a file.
- The bot deletes the AI metadata and returns a clean MP4.
- H.264 video is not recompressed: frames match the original, same quality.
## Good to know
- Files up to 50 MB.
- You can also send a TikTok video link — the bot downloads it in original quality.
- If a clip is fully generated, TikTok’s rules may require you to disclose it manually.

articles.title: What is C2PA (Content Credentials) and how to remove it from photos and videos
articles.desc: In plain words: what C2PA stores, which apps write it, why social networks use it to add an AI label, and how to remove this data from a file.
articles.body:
C2PA is a standard for a file’s “provenance passport”. A signed record is embedded in the photo or video: which app made it, how it was edited, whether AI was used. It is also called Content Credentials.
## Who writes C2PA
- Image and video generators, for example Adobe Firefly and OpenAI services.
- Editors with AI features: generative fill, object removal.
- Some cameras and phones.
## Why it matters
- Instagram, Facebook and TikTok read C2PA and use it to add an AI label.
- The record stays in the file even after renaming or forwarding it.
## How to remove C2PA
- Send the photo or video to [@AIMediaclean_bot](https://t.me/AIMediaclean_bot?start=blog_en_c2pa).
- The bot deletes the C2PA (JUMBF) blocks plus EXIF, XMP and IPTC, and verifies the file structure.
- Photos keep their size, H.264 videos keep the original quality.
## What C2PA removal does not do
- It does not remove visible watermarks or marks drawn into the image itself.
